headline: Approved $2,125,684 water/sewer loan, $1,675,000 Zetron radio system loan, non-union pay ordinance, and two secondhand dealer licenses.
summary: The Council approved loan authorizations for water/street/sewer work and a Zetron Max alerting/radio control system, along with an ordinance amending pay charts for non-union employees. It also approved secondhand dealer licenses, a fitness equipment and grant acceptance, and several resolutions, while referring other licenses and special permit modifications to committees.
decisions: Approved the regular City Council meeting minutes of August 13, 2026.
Approved the McDevitt Eighth Grade Civic Sidewalk Project Resolution.
Approved the Secondhand Dealers license at 56 Felton Street for More Than Words.
Referred the Secondhand Dealers license at 85 River Street for Pedals & Powder, LLC to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
Referred the Fuel Storage license at 245 Fifth Avenue for ALP PHOP Manager LLC to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
Referred the Special Permit Modification at 287 Crescent Street for Dyer's Crescent Suites, LLC to the Ordinances and Rules Committee and continued the hearing to November 23, 2026.
Referred the Special Permit Modification at 995 Main Street for Service Credit Union to the Ordinances and Rules Committee and continued the hearing to November 23, 2026.
Referred the Veterans' housing concept plan presentation request to the Committee of the Whole.
Referred acceptance of fitness equipment from Core Development & Management and Planet Fitness to the Finance Committee.
Referred acceptance of the Green Communities Competitive Grant of $173,714 to the Finance Committee.
Approved acceptance of a $208,096 grant from the Massachusetts Executive Office of Aging and Independence for the Council on Aging.
Approved a $98,672.05 transfer for the construction phase of the Green Infrastructure Retrofit Project at the Embassy Garage.
Referred the Class 2 License renewal at 215 Lexington Street for New England Transit Sales, Inc. to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
Approved the National Hispanic Heritage Month Resolution.
Approved the request to invite the Director of Information Technology to the Committee of the Whole on AI use, and referred the matter to the Committee of the Whole.
Referred the Secondhand Dealers License Resolution to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
Referred the Rule 95 Utility Master Plan Resolution to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
Referred the Resolution Amending the MBTA Communities Zoning Ordinance to Incorporate the City's Newly Adopted Inclusionary Zoning Requirements to the Ordinances and Rules Committee.
Approved the Yolanda Cellucci Resolution.
Referred the letter on naming the 617 Lexington Street building 'The John J "Jack" Daddona Education Center' to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
Approved the $2,125,684 Water/Street/Sewer Loan Authorization on second and final reading, 13-0-1-1.
Approved the $1,675,000 Zetron Max alerting/radio control system Loan Authorization on second and final reading, 13-0-1-1.
Approved the Compensation Ordinance amending pay charts for non-union employees on third and final reading, 12-0-1-1-1.

plain_text:
1
Waltham City Council 
Minutes of the Meeting of 
September 14, 2026
President Logan called the meeting to order at 7:32 p.m. 
 
Artie Kronenfeld from the Waltham Times was recognized as recording the meeting.
Present: Bradley-MacArthur, Brasco, Durkee, Harris, Hanley, Katz, King, LaCava, LaFauci, 
LeBlanc, McLaughlin, Tzioumis, Vidal and President Logan. 
Absent: Dunn.
City Clerk Vizard recited the Council Prayer followed by President Logan leading all present in the 
Pledge of Allegiance. Councillor Durkee spoke on September, being Suicide Prevention Month and
asked for a moment of silence for all the military that have served past and present.
Councillor LeBlanc moved approval of the regular City Council meeting minutes of August 13, 
2026. The motion was approved by a voice vote. 
President Logan relinquished the Chair to Vice President LeBlanc.
President Logan made a motion that was approved by a voice vote to suspend Rule 8 to take the 
McDevitt Eighth Grade Civic Sidewalk Project Resolution out of order. President Logan spoke 
on the Resolution. President Logan made a motion that was approved by a voice vote to suspend 
Rule 9 to hear from off committee members. McDevitt Middle School Eighth Grade Civics 
teacher, Mr. Hanlon, spoke on the project. President Logan presented the Resolutions to Mr. 
Hanlon and the students involved on the project. President Logan moved to suspend Rule 39 to 
act on the matter without Committee reference. The motion was approved by a voice vote. 
President Logan moved approval of the matter. The motion was approved by a voice vote and 
the McDevitt Eighth Grade Civic Sidewalk Project Resolution was approved.
Vice President LeBlanc relinquished the Chair back to President Logan.
Clerk Vizard read Rule 86.
First Public Hearing: Secondhand Dealers license at 56 Felton Street for More Than Words
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Shiricka Brown of 56 Felton Street, Waltham, MA 
representing the petitioner, spoke on the matter. With no one else in favor, no one in opposition 
and no one in a neutral position to the license President Logan closed that part of the public 
hearing and opened the hearing up to questions from Councillors. Councillors Katz, Bradley-
MacArthur Vidal, McLaughlin and LeBlanc asked questions. Ms. Brown provided answers. 
Councillor Vidal made a motion to suspend Rule 39 to act on the matter without Committee 
reference. The motion was approved by a voice vote. Councillor Vidal moved for approval of the
matter. The motion was approved by a voice vote and the Secondhand Dealers license for More 
than Words at 56 Felton Street was approved.
Second Public Hearing: Secondhand Dealers license at 85 River Street for Pedals & Powder, LLC
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Kendall Howard, 9 Addison Street, Arlington, MA 
representing the petitioner, spoke on the matter. With no one else in favor, no one in opposition and 
no one in a neutral position to the license, President Logan closed that part of the public hearing and 
opened the hearing up to questions from Councillors. Councillors LaCava, Bradley-MacArthur,
2
Vidal and LaFauci asked questions. Mr. Howard provided answers. With no further questions 
President Logan closed the Public Hearing and referred the matter to the Licenses and Franchises 
Committee.
Third Public Hearing: Fuel Storage license at 245 Fifth Avenue for ALP PHOP Manager LLC
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Paul Finger of 14 Spring Street, Waltham, MA 
representing the petitioner, spoke on the matter. With no one else in favor, no one in opposition and 
no one in a neutral position to the license, President Logan closed that part of the public hearing and 
opened the hearing up to questions from Councillors. Councillor LaFauci spoke on the matter. With 
no further questions President Logan closed the Public Hearing and referred the matter to the 
Licenses and Franchises Committee.
Fourth Public Hearing: Special Permit Modification at 287 Crescent Street for Dyer’s Crescent 
Suites, LLC.
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Kevin Leitner representing the petitioner, spoke on the 
matter. With no one else in favor, no one in opposition and no one in a neutral position to the 
modification, President Logan closed that part of the public hearing and opened the hearing up to 
questions from Councillors. Councillors Harris and LaCava spoke on the matter. With no further 
questions President Logan referred the matter to the Ordinances and Rules Committee. President 
Logan recessed the Public Hearing to date certain of Monday, November 23, 2026 at 7:30 p.m.
Fifth Public Hearing: Special Permit Modification at 995 Main Street for Service Credit Union
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Attorney Michael Connors of 689 Main Street, 
Waltham, MA representing the petitioner, spoke on the matter. With no one else in favor, no one in 
opposition and no one in a neutral position to the modification, President Logan closed that part of 
the public hearing and opened the hearing up to questions from Councillors. Councillors LaFauci 
and King spoke on the matter. With no further questions President Logan referred the matter to the 
Ordinances and Rules Committee. President Logan recessed the Public Hearing to date certain of 
Monday, November 23, 2026 at 7:30 p.m.
Communications from the Mayor
1. The Mayor respectfully requested an opportunity for a presentation of a concept plan for 
Veterans’ housing and services by Caritas Communities, Veterans’ Pathway, and the city 
team on September 21, 2026. Referred to the Committee of the Whole.
2. The Mayor respectfully requested approval of the acceptance of fitness equipment from 
Core Development & Management and Planet Fitness for the City of Waltham Fire 
Department. Referred to the Finance Committee.
3. The Mayor respectfully requested acceptance of the Green Communities Competitive 
Grant in the amount of $173,714 from the Department of Energy Resources (DOER) 
Green Communities Division. Referred to the Finance Committee.
4. The Mayor respectfully requested acceptance of a grant in the amount of $208,096 from 
the Massachusetts Executive Office of Aging and Independence to be used by the Council 
on Aging. Councillor Katz made a motion to suspend Rule 39 to act on the matter without 
Committee reference. The motion was approved by a voice vote. Councillor Katz made a 
motion for approval. The motion was approved by a voice vote
3
5. The Mayor respectfully requested without Committee reference a transfer in the amount of
$98,672.05 towards the construction phase of the Green Infrastructure Retrofit Project at 
the Embassy Garage. Councillor Katz made a motion to suspend Rule 39 to act on the 
matter without Committee reference. The motion was approved by a voice vote. 
Councillor Katz made a motion that was approved by a voice vote to suspend Rule 9 to 
hear from off committee member City Engineer Robert Winn. Engineer Winn spoke on 
the matter. Councillor LaFauci spoke on the matter. Councillor Katz moved approval of 
the matter. The motion was approved by a voice vote
Applications and Licenses
All Applications and Licenses referred to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
1.  Class 2 License renewal – 215 Lexington Street – New England Transit Sales, Inc.
Resolutions, Orders and Ordinances
 National Hispanic Heritage Month Resolution
Clerk Vizard read the Resolution. Councillor Vidal spoke on the Resolution. Councillor 
Vidal moved to suspend Rule 39 to act on the matter without Committee reference. The 
motion was approved by a voice vote. Councillor Vidal moved approval. The motion was 
approved by a voice vote and the National Hispanic Heritage Month Resolution was 
approved.
 Use of Artificial Intelligence in City Government
Clerk Vizard read the Resolution. Councillor Vidal spoke on the Resolution. Councillor 
Vidal made a request that the Director of Information Technology be invited to appear 
before the Committee of the Whole to discuss the City’s current use of artificial intelligence 
technologies, any existing policies, practices, or safeguards relating to their use, and 
considerations regarding the responsible use of artificial intelligence in municipal 
operations. Further, the Director discuss any recommendations or guidance he may have for 
the City Council as the City considers the opportunities and potential risks associated with 
the use of artificial intelligence. The request was approved by a voice vote. Referred to the 
Committee of the Whole.
 McDevitt 8th Grade Civic Sidewalk Project Resolution
This matter was disposed of earlier in the evening
 Secondhand Dealers License Resolution
Clerk Vizard read the Resolution. Referred to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
 Rule 95 Utility Master Plan Resolution
Clerk Vizard read the Resolution. Councillor Katz spoke on the matter. Referred to the 
Licenses and Franchises Committee.
 Resolution Amending the MBTA Communities Zoning Ordinance to Incorporate the City’s 
Newly Adopted Inclusionary Zoning Requirements
Clerk Vizard read the Resolution. Referred to the Ordinances and Rules Committee.
 Yolanda Resolution
Clerk Vizard read the Resolution. Councillor Hanley spoke on the Resolution and asked for 
a moment of silence in honor of Yolanda. Councillor Hanley moved to suspend Rule 39 to 
act on the matter without Committee reference. The motion was approved by a voice vote. 
Councillor Hanley moved for approval. The motion was approved by a voice vote and the 
Yolanda Cellucci Resolution was approved.
4
Unfinished Business & Other Business
 Letter from the Waltham School Committee regarding naming of 617 Lexington Street 
building “The John J “Jack” Daddona Education Center”
Referred to the Licenses and Franchises Committee
Tabled Items
 66 Brewster Road (Tabled 6/9/25)
 Loan Authorization $2,125,684 Water/Street/ Sewer (1st reading 8/3/26)
Councillor Katz made a motion that was approved by a voice vote to take the matter off 
the table. Councillor Katz made a motion for a second and final reading of the matter. Roll
Call required.
In favor: Councillors Bradley-MacArthur, Brasco, Durkee, Hanley, Harris, Katz, King, 
LaCava, LaFauci, LeBlanc, McLaughlin, Tzioumis and Vidal
Opposed: None.
Absent: Dunn.
Presiding: Logan.
Approved: 13-0-1-1.
 Loan Authorization $1,675,000 Zetron Max alerting/radio control system (1st reading 
8/3/26)
Councillor Katz made a motion that was approved by a voice vote to take the matter off 
the table. Councillor Katz made a motion for a second and final reading of the matter. Roll
Call required.
In favor: Councillors Bradley-MacArthur, Brasco, Durkee, Hanley, Harris, Katz, King, 
LaCava, LaFauci, LeBlanc, McLaughlin, Tzioumis and Vidal
Opposed: None.
Absent: Dunn.
Presiding: Logan.
Approved: 13-0-1-1.
 Compensation Ordinance to amend the existing pay charts for non-union employees (1st
Reading 8/3/26)
Councillor King recused himself. Councillor Harris made a motion that was approved by a
voice vote to take the matter off the table. Councillor Harris made a motion that was 
approved by a voice vote for a second reading. Councillor Harris made a motion to 
suspend Rule 39 to act on the matter without Committee reference. The motion was 
approved by a voice vote. Councillor Harris made a motion for a third and final reading of 
the matter. Roll Call required.
In favor: Councillors Bradley-MacArthur, Brasco, Durkee, Hanley, Harris, Katz, LaCava, 
LaFauci, LeBlanc, McLaughlin, Tzioumis and Vidal
Opposed: None.
Recused: King.
Absent: Dunn.
Presiding: Logan.
Approved: 12-0-1-1-1.
Councillor Katz rose to wish all the Jewish residents of Waltham a Happy Rosh Hashanah and 
Yom Kippur. Councillor Katz recited a small prayer.
5
With no further matters Councillor LaFauci made a motion to adjourn. The motion was approved
by a voice vote. President Logan declared the meeting adjourned at 9:13 p.m.
Respectfully submitted by:
Cathy Magliarditi
Executive Assistant to the City Clerk
September 21, 2026
